answer.rationale: The 18% cut mandate is hard, primary supply expires in 14 days, and the low-cost vendor's quote alone meets it—this dominates on TCO. I choose not to pull an archive because my only real hesitation is unrecorded downside from switching a primary source at scale, and the memories that speak to that are ambiguous: memory_c2 says a prior switch was fast and invoicing clean, but memory_c3 exists precisely because a single-source position failed once before, and memory_c1 suggests incumbent continuity has had real value. That tension in the record lowers my confidence that past smooth switching will repeat, and the 94% line with no buffer makes me less willing to bet on it. Still, given one available decision, the expiring contract forces a choice, and the cheapest defensible path is a guarded switch: execute the low-cost vendor as primary but keep volume ramped, protect the first cycle with whatever residual incumbent capacity or expedited terms can be secured, and flag delivery risk explicitly for next-cycle review. If verification had been available without cost, I would have pulled memory_c2 to see whether the prior switch's quick onboarding involved comparable volume, lead time, and assembly-line exposure.
